pages.title: libcephfs, ceph-fuse and NFS-Ganesha: what the userspace client requires from an MDS

features.name: Session open with client metadata
features.description: REQUEST_OPEN (MClientSession v7) carries metadata hostname, pid, entity_id, root, ceph_version, ceph_sha1, client_metadata overrides, mount_point (ceph-fuse), uuid and timeout (Ganesha), supported_features, metric_spec.
features.notes: Sessions are opened lazily by the first request to a rank; mount GETATTRs walk from the mount root up to / .

features.name: CephFS feature-bit negotiation
features.description: libcephfs advertises CEPHFS_FEATURES_ALL (bits 0-24) and switches encodings on the MDS bits received in CEPH_SESSION_OPEN (REPLY_ENCODING, 32BITS_RETRY_FWD, HAS_OWNER_UIDGID, DELEG_INO, MULTI_RECONNECT, NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO, OP_GETVXATTR, BLOCKDIFF, RECLAIM_CLIENT, METRIC_COLLECT).
features.notes: client_debug_inject_features overrides the advertised set. The client picks decoders from the MDS bits it received (not from message content) and never tests the MDS's MDS_AUTH_CAPS_CHECK bit; cap_auths from OPEN are used whenever present.

features.name: Cap renewal and cap TTL
features.description: REQUEST_RENEWCAPS every session_timeout/3 to ranks >= REJOIN; caps and leases are valid only until last_cap_renew_request + session_timeout after a matching RENEWCAPS ack.
features.notes: Delayed acks make cached attributes unusable and push load back to the MDS.

features.name: Stale session handling
features.description: CEPH_SESSION_STALE bumps cap_gen and invalidates all caps/leases of the session; remote connection reset marks the session STALE (or closes it with client_reconnect_stale).

features.name: Session close with push sequence
features.description: REQUEST_CLOSE carries the count of MClientCaps/Lease/Snap/Quota messages received; re-sent on every new push while CLOSING; unmount waits up to client_shutdown_timeout.

features.name: Session reject handling
features.description: CEPH_SESSION_REJECT closes the session as REJECTED; requests to that rank fail with -EPERM; error_string logged, flags ignored.

features.name: Forced read-only session
features.description: CEPH_SESSION_FORCE_RO marks the session readonly; acquiring Fw on inodes whose auth cap is on it fails with -EROFS.

features.name: Cap recall (RECALL_STATE) and cache trimming
features.description: RECALL_STATE triggers renew + cap-release flush, then trim_caps(max_caps): drop non-auth caps, trim dentries, call the application's ino_release_cb, invalidate kernel dcache for ceph-fuse.
features.notes: Ganesha holds ll references; caps are freed only after it drops them.

features.name: FLUSHMSG / FLUSHMSG_ACK
features.description: On FLUSHMSG the client sends queued cap releases then FLUSHMSG_ACK with the same seq.

features.name: MDS journal flush request
features.description: REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG sent on fsync of inodes with unsafe ops, on syncfs and at unmount (only to Luminous+ MDS connections).
features.notes: Used for fsync/fsyncdir/syncfs durability. The C++ MDS only flushes on REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG while the rank is ACTIVE (src/mds/Server.cc:883-885).

features.name: MDS target selection
features.description: choose_target_mds: explicit/forwarded rank, dirfrag hash with dl_dir_hash via fragmap/frag_repmap, auth cap for writes/open/readdir/rstat/xattr getattr, any cap otherwise, random up rank as fallback; LOOKUPINO/PARENT/NAME/HASH to rand() % num_in.

features.name: Request encoding
features.description: MClientRequest v6 with head v1/v2/v3 (or legacy without FS_BTIME), embedded cap/dentry-lease releases, mdsmap epoch, osdmap epoch for SETXATTR, gid list, owner uid/gid for inode-creating ops, alternate_name, fscrypt_auth/file; paths relative to inode numbers.

features.name: Request forwarding
features.description: MClientRequestForward makes the client resend to dest_mds; num_fwd must strictly increase, else -EMULTIHOP; retry counters limited (256 for old MDS).
features.notes: kick_requests at rank ACTIVE never re-sends anything (retry_attempt==0 implies mds==-1); requests are re-driven by the RECONNECT-time resend and by callers woken from waiting_for_mdsmap.

features.name: Early (unsafe) and safe replies
features.description: Caller is woken on the first reply; unsafe requests tracked per session, parent dir and target inode until the safe reply; safe reply after unsafe must carry no trace.
features.notes: fsync/syncfs wait on waitfor_safe of unsafe requests.

features.name: Reply trace decoding and cache merge
features.description: InodeStat v9 / LeaseStat v2 / DirStat v1 decoding (versioned with REPLY_ENCODING), version and cap-gated attribute merge, snap trace application, I_COMPLETE on empty dirs.

features.name: Traceless reply recovery and created-ino
features.description: extra_bl of 8+ bytes in create-type replies carries the created ino, decoded as openc_response_t whenever the MDS advertised DELEG_INO and as a raw u64 otherwise (delegated inos discarded); traceless replies are followed by LOOKUP or forced GETATTR; ino mismatch gives -EINTR; a traceless reply whose request dentry is unlinked hits ceph_abort_msg.
features.notes: The C++ MDS encodes openc_response_t only if mds_allow_async_dirops is also true (src/mds/Server.cc:2591-2614), otherwise a raw u64: with mds_allow_async_dirops=false libcephfs would mis-decode (code-level observation).

features.name: Dentry leases
features.description: Leases from LeaseStat (ttl from request send time, gen = session cap_gen); MDS REVOKE answered with RELEASE; no renew.

features.name: Directory completeness and negative dentries
features.description: With Fs on a directory, cached dentries with matching shared_gen are valid and ENOENT can be concluded locally when I_COMPLETE.

features.name: Readdir protocol
features.description: READDIR per frag with CEPH_READDIR_REPLY_BITFLAGS, resume by last name or offset_hash, max_entries/max_bytes 0, hash-order offsets computed client-side, -EAGAIN retry, I_COMPLETE marking.

features.name: Caps for file IO and max_size
features.description: get_caps waits for Fr/Fw (+Fc/Fb wanted); writes beyond max_size request a larger max_size from the auth MDS and block until granted.

features.name: Cap update and flush
features.description: Single op CEPH_CAP_OP_UPDATE carries issued/implemented, wanted, dirty bits, flush tid, oldest_flush_tid, FLAG_SYNC/FLAG_PENDING_CAPSNAP, osd barrier, caller uid/gid -1; FLUSH_ACK clears flush tids.

features.name: Cap release
features.description: Batched MClientCapRelease v2 per session flushed each tick, on FLUSHMSG or immediately for unknown inodes/caps; request-embedded releases with drop/unless masks; client_caps_release_delay before releasing unused caps.

features.name: Cap import/export
features.description: EXPORT with peer info pre-creates the target cap (opening a session if needed); IMPORT installs the auth cap, removes the old one and re-sends pending flushes.
features.notes: FLUSHSNAP_ACK is dispatched before the per-rank cap check and handle_cap_flushsnap_ack asserts the client holds a cap from the sending rank; add_update_cap asserts cap_id is unchanged when a cap's seq does not advance.

features.name: Cap snaps (FLUSHSNAP)
features.description: New snapshots in a realm create CapSnaps for dirty/writing inodes; flushed with CEPH_CAP_OP_FLUSHSNAP after data writeback; acked by FLUSHSNAP_ACK.

features.name: Buffered setattr under exclusive caps
features.description: uid/gid/mode/btime/fscrypt_auth buffered under Ax; size growth and times under Fx; forward times under Fw; only if MDS auth caps can be checked locally; else SETATTR.

features.name: Client-side MDS auth caps enforcement
features.description: cap_auths from CEPH_SESSION_OPEN evaluated by mds_check_access (path, uid/gids, root_squash, rw) before buffered setattr and cap-only opens.

features.name: Snap realms and snap traces
features.description: SnapRealmInfoNew (with NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO) or SnapRealmInfo traces in replies, caps and MClientSnap; SPLIT moves inodes and child realms; realm parents re-verified.
features.notes: SPLIT asserts head.split != 0 and that the first realm record of the trace is head.split (src/client/Client.cc:5636-5640).

features.name: Snapshot namespace ops
features.description: .snap synthesized locally; LOOKUPSNAP, LSSNAP, MKSNAP (with metadata), RMSNAP, RENAMESNAP; snapshot inodes read-only.

features.name: Snapshot metadata, snapdiff and blockdiff
features.description: CEPH_MDS_OP_SNAP_METADATA, READDIR_SNAPDIFF and FILE_BLOCKDIFF (needs BLOCKDIFF feature) used by cephfs-mirror and mgr.

features.name: Client-side quota enforcement
features.description: max_files/max_bytes checked against rstat of quota roots found via the snap realm chain; EDQUOT, EXDEV for cross-quota renames; MClientQuota updates; quota dirs must be realm roots.

features.name: statfs with quota
features.description: statfs from monitor pool stats, or quota max_bytes/rbytes of the quota root after a forced GETATTR.

features.name: Advisory file locks
features.description: fcntl and flock via SETFILELOCK/GETFILELOCK (owner bit 63), blocking waits at the MDS, interrupt via *_INTR unlock, lock state replayed in MClientReconnect.

features.name: MDS failover reconnect
features.description: On RECONNECT: resend unsafe requests with REPLAY, resend sent requests without releases, early cap flushes, MClientReconnect (caps with short path, wanted/issued, realm, snap_follows, flock blob; multi-part with MULTI_RECONNECT).

features.name: Blocklist and eviction handling
features.description: OSDMap blocklist aborts requests with -EBLOCKLISTED and closes sessions; client_reconnect_stale enables periodic auto-reconnect; closed sessions drop caps and unsafe requests with -EIO.

features.name: Client metrics
features.description: MClientMetrics to rank 0 every tick (latencies, cap/dentry-lease hit rates, opened files/inodes, pinned caps, IO sizes, per-subvolume IO metrics) filtered by MDS metric_spec.

features.name: Session reclaim by uuid
features.description: ceph_start_reclaim sends MClientReclaim(uuid, CEPH_RECLAIM_RESET) to every rank 0..num_in-1 (after opening sparse-metadata sessions); the MDS kills or evicts+blocklists the old session with the same uuid and auth_name and replies with OSDMap epoch and the old address (none if no match, client then returns -ENOENT). ceph_finish_reclaim sends FLAG_FINISH only after a non-RESET reclaim (which the current MDS rejects with -EINVAL), so with RESET it sends nothing; ceph_set_uuid closes all sessions so mount reopens them with the uuid.
features.notes: ceph_set_uuid/ceph_set_session_timeout ceph_assert that ceph_init was called. set_uuid waits up to client_shutdown_timeout for CEPH_SESSION_CLOSE, which the MDS only sends once the rank is ACTIVE.

features.name: Session timeout override
features.description: Session metadata 'timeout' (ceph_set_session_timeout): in find_idle_sessions, after the normal queue_max_age+session_timeout cutoff and the session_autoclose eviction check (which applies regardless of timeout), and only if the MDS is revoking caps or awaiting a flush from the session (mds_defer_session_stale, default true), the session is not marked stale but evicted once silent for queue_max_age+timeout (0 = never by this rule); during recovery it is kept in client_reclaim_gather, holding the rank in CLIENTREPLAY until reclaimed or killed.

features.name: NFS delegations on top of caps
features.description: ceph_ll_delegation grants RD/WR delegations when the needed caps are already issued; recalled on cap revocation or local conflicting opens/namespace ops; unreturned delegations force-unmount the client after deleg_timeout.

features.name: Lookup by inode number
features.description: ceph_ll_lookup_inode/ceph_ll_lookup_vino send LOOKUPINO (with snapid) to rank rand() % num_in with the cmount default perms; '..' without cached parent sends LOOKUPPARENT (random rank); LOOKUPNAME is only sent by the unused Client::lookup_name and a getcwd fallback; ceph-fuse uses LOOKUPINO (with the FUSE caller's perms) for unknown parents.
features.notes: Needed for NFS file handles and FUSE export support.

features.name: Handle-based low-level API
features.description: ceph_ll_* operate on Inode handles; requests are built relative to inode numbers; handle-only inodes cannot buffer setattr or open locally.

features.name: fsync and sync-write semantics
features.description: fsync flushes data to OSDs, sends a synchronous cap flush (FLAG_SYNC) for dirty metadata, flushes MDS logs for unsafe ops and waits for safe replies and FLUSH_ACK; O_SYNC/O_DSYNC only flush data.

features.name: Nonblocking IO for Ganesha
features.description: ceph_ll_nonblocking_readv_writev / ceph_ll_nonblocking_fsync complete via callbacks; cap waits still block the caller thread.

features.name: ceph-fuse operation mapping and fake inode numbers
features.description: FUSE low-level ops mapped to ll_* calls; FUSE inode = (snap tag << 48) | ino; kernel cache coherence via notify_inval_inode / notify_delete / remount.
features.notes: Inode numbers must fit in 48 bits.

features.name: POSIX ACLs (client side)
features.description: With client_acl_type=posix_acl, default ACLs are evaluated at create and sent as an xattr blob in the create request; chmod rewrites the access ACL via SETXATTR.

features.name: Charmap name wrapping
features.description: In charmap directories the client validates UTF-8, normalizes and case-folds names and sends the original as alternate_name (requires CHARMAP feature at the MDS).

features.name: fscrypt support
features.description: Encrypted names (alternate_name), fscrypt_auth/fscrypt_file in requests and caps, CEPH_SETATTR_FSCRYPT_* masks and last-block payload in SETATTR truncation.

features.name: Quarantine awareness
features.description: QUARANTINE feature: cap grants with oserrno -EQUARANTINED mark inodes quarantined; MQuarantineDisable clears it; readdir tolerates -EACCES for quarantined entries.

features.name: Inline data
features.description: First IO forces GETATTR(Fs|Fr) to learn inline_version; small writes update inline data under Fb; larger writes uninline via OSD ops.

features.name: LazyIO
features.description: CEPH_O_LAZY / ceph_lazyio change open mode to include Fl; buffered IO allowed under Fl.

features.name: MDS admin commands via libcephfs
features.description: ceph_mds_command resolves MDS specs against the FSMap and sends MCommand directly to daemons.

features.name: Virtual xattrs
features.description: ceph.dir.*/ceph.file.layout*/ceph.quota* computed locally after a forced GETATTR; other ceph.* names fetched with GETVXATTR; layout pool changes wait for the latest OSDMap and carry the osdmap epoch.

features.name: Shared libcephfs mounts via libcephfsd (Samba)
features.description: mgr/smb can configure Samba vfs_ceph_new with proxy=yes; the in-tree libcephfsd daemon runs real libcephfs mounts and shares one mount among client processes with identical configuration, so one MDS session per rank multiplexes several SMB server processes.
features.notes: Samba's VFS module itself is not in this repository.

features.name: Request tid ordering on the wire
features.description: tids are assigned at make_request entry but a request may wait for an MDSMap or session open, or be forwarded/re-sent, so one session's requests can reach a rank out of tid order; on reconnect unsafe requests go first (unsafe-reply order), then other sent requests in tid order.

serialization_points.name: Client::client_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: entire client: cache, caps, sessions, requests, ObjectCacher
serialization_points.why_serialized: one coarse mutex protects all client state
serialization_points.notes: Ganesha requests to all exports sharing a cmount are prepared and completed under one lock; MDS sees one session per rank with bursty concurrency.

serialization_points.name: Single ms_dispatch thread with reply kickback
serialization_points.why_serialized: dispatch thread waits until the caller consumed the reply
serialization_points.notes: Replies/caps from all ranks are processed sequentially; slow callers delay all MDS message processing of the client.

serialization_points.name: oldest_client_tid gating
serialization_points.why_serialized: MDS may only trim completed requests below the oldest outstanding client tid
serialization_points.notes: Blocking SETFILELOCK excluded; one stuck request pins the whole session's completed-request list.

serialization_points.name: Push-sequence accounting for close
serialization_points.why_serialized: MDS ignores REQUEST_CLOSE until client acknowledged all counted pushes

serialization_points.name: Cap flush tid ordering
serialization_points.why_serialized: FLUSH_ACK for tid N completes all earlier tids of the inode; oldest_flush_tid lets the MDS trim

serialization_points.name: Reconnect ordering
serialization_points.why_serialized: replays and early cap flushes must reach the MDS before the cap reconnect message

serialization_points.name: fsync waits for MDS journal
serialization_points.shared_state: dirty caps and unsafe ops of the inode
serialization_points.why_serialized: metadata durability requires journal flush on the rank(s) holding unsafe ops and the auth cap
serialization_points.notes: Only the journal(s) containing the inode's updates need flushing; REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG flushes the whole rank log in the C++ MDS.

serialization_points.name: Rank stays in CLIENTREPLAY for timeout sessions
serialization_points.why_serialized: rank cannot go ACTIVE until Ganesha sessions with 'timeout' metadata are reclaimed or killed
serialization_points.notes: libcephfs sends requests only to ACTIVE/STOPPING ranks, so all clients of the rank wait for one Ganesha reclaim.

serialization_points.name: Delegation break on open
serialization_points.why_serialized: local conflicting open blocks until delegations are returned; remote conflicts wait for cap revocation

serialization_points.name: Session-wide cap validity
serialization_points.why_serialized: a single late RENEWCAPS ack invalidates every cap of the session

serialization_points.name: Blocking file-lock requests
serialization_points.shared_state: inode lock state at the MDS
serialization_points.why_serialized: wait=1 SETFILELOCK requests stay outstanding at the MDS until granted

serialization_points.name: Session close gated on rank ACTIVE (set_uuid)
serialization_points.why_serialized: REQUEST_CLOSE is deferred until the rank is ACTIVE; ceph_set_uuid waits for CEPH_SESSION_CLOSE from every rank (client_shutdown_timeout)
serialization_points.notes: A rank held in CLIENTREPLAY by other pending 'timeout' sessions makes a restarting Ganesha's set_uuid time out (derived from code).

external_contract.detail: MClientSession v7: metadata map (hostname, pid, entity_id, root, ceph_version, ceph_sha1, mount_point, uuid, timeout, client_metadata extras), supported_features = bits 0..24, metric_spec = metric types 0..16.
Must carry supported_features (replace client view), metric_spec flags, cap_auths; seq adopted if client seq is 0; may be re-sent for an open session (features refreshed).
OPEN, CLOSE, RENEWCAPS, STALE, RECALL_STATE, FLUSHMSG, FORCE_RO, REJECT; anything else triggers ceph_abort().

REQUEST_OPEN (v7), REQUEST_RENEWCAPS (v1, seq), REQUEST_CLOSE (v1, push seq), FLUSHMSG_ACK (v1), REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG (v1, only to Luminous+ connections); oldest_client_tid never on the wire for RENEWCAPS.
Client counts MClientCaps, MClientLease, MClientSnap, MClientQuota; REQUEST_CLOSE seq must equal MDS push_seq for the close to be accepted.

ceph_mds_request_head version 1 without 32BITS_RETRY_FWD, 2 without HAS_OWNER_UIDGID, else 3 with struct_len and owner uid/gid; legacy head when connection lacks FS_BTIME; MClientRequest v6 body always.
filepath base is an inode number (#ino/name), including snapped inodes resolved through their non-snap ancestor with empty components for .snap.
ceph_mds_request_release records (ino, cap_id, caps, wanted, seq, issue_seq, mseq, dname_seq, dname) inside requests; dropped for requests re-sent during RECONNECT.
LOOKUP and dentry-bearing requests set CEPH_MDS_FLAG_WANT_DENTRY; ENOENT replies should include the null dentry trace and lease so the client caches the negative dentry.
Requests that got an unsafe reply are re-sent during RECONNECT with CEPH_MDS_FLAG_REPLAY and head.ino = target ino and no releases.
MClientRequestForward.num_fwd must be > previous num_fwd for the request, else the request aborts with -EMULTIHOP; client always resends to dest_mds.
Reply must come from the rank the request was last sent to; second unsafe reply ignored; safe-after-unsafe must have empty trace (assert).
Payload = head, trace_bl, extra_bl, snapbl with no trailing bytes (ceph_assert(p.end())).

Versioned InodeStat up to v9 when REPLY_ENCODING: cap with AUTH flag, inline_version (>0), change_attr, dir_layout hash, dirfragtree, rstat, quota, dir_pin, snap_btime, rsnaps, snap_metadata, fscrypt_auth/file, optmetadata (charmap, quarantine), subvolume_id.

Create-type replies carry the created ino in extra_bl; libcephfs decodes 8+ bytes as openc_response_t whenever the MDS advertised DELEG_INO, else as raw u64, so an MDS advertising DELEG_INO must always use openc_response_t; client ignores delegated_inos.
extra_bl = DirStat, u32 count, u16 flags (FRAG_END, HASH_ORDER, OFFSET_HASH), entries (name, LeaseStat, InodeStat) sorted by (frag_value(hash), name); max_entries/max_bytes 0 in requests.
CEPH_CAP_OP_UPDATE (dirty bits = flush, FLAG_SYNC, FLAG_PENDING_CAPSNAP, max_size request, oldest_flush_tid, caller uid/gid -1, osd_epoch_barrier) and CEPH_CAP_OP_FLUSHSNAP; MClientCaps v14.
GRANT, REVOKE, TRUNC, EXPORT (peer), IMPORT (peer, snap trace), FLUSH_ACK (client tid), FLUSHSNAP_ACK (follows+tid); osd_epoch_barrier pauses OSD IO; subvolume_id; oserrno -EQUARANTINED.

Every REVOKE is answered with a cap UPDATE: immediately, after flushing buffered data, or after invalidating cache; caps still referenced (delegations, in-flight IO) delay the ack until the reference is dropped; unknown inode/cap -> immediate MClientCapRelease.
MClientCapRelease v2: items {ino, cap_id, migrate_seq, issue_seq} + osd_epoch_barrier; sent each tick to ranks in CLIENTREPLAY/ACTIVE/STOPPING; queue discarded at reconnect.
MDS may only send CEPH_MDS_LEASE_REVOKE (assert); client replies CEPH_MDS_LEASE_RELEASE with same seq/mask/ino/first/last/dname; no renew.

Strict decode; SPLIT with split ino/realm lists and head.split as first trace realm; libcephfs decodes SnapRealmInfoNew iff the MDS advertised NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO, while the C++ MDS encodes it iff the client advertised it, so an MDS must advertise the bit exactly when it sends the new format to libcephfs.
Strict decode {ino, rctime, rbytes, rfiles, rsubdirs, quota}; replaces client quota and rstat.
After setting ceph.quota.* the inode must be its own snap realm root in the reply's snap trace, else setxattr returns -EOPNOTSUPP to the application.

v5 multi-part (more flag) with MULTI_RECONNECT, else v3/v2/v1 by connection features; caps keyed by ino with cap_id, pathbase+dname (or #ino with empty name), wanted, issued (PIN if stale), realm, snap_follows, flock blob (u32 n + ceph_filelock for fcntl then flock; empty when the inode never had lock state); realms {ino, seq, parent}.
Unsafe replays (REPLAY) and already-sent requests (retry_attempt>0, no releases) are re-sent before MClientReconnect; early cap flushes for revoked flushing caps also precede it.

Client reads rank states, addrs, incarnation, max_mds, num_in, session_timeout, session_autoclose, max_filesize, data_pools, fs_name, refuse_client_session flag, export_targets; sends requests only to ACTIVE/STOPPING ranks.
Client opens sessions to a rank's export_targets (from MDSMap mds_info) once that rank is open/active.

Reclaim(uuid, CEPH_RECLAIM_RESET) per rank 0..num_in-1; reply result, OSDMap epoch, old session addrs (none and epoch 0 when no session matched); FLAG_FINISH (1<<31) must be alone and is only sent by libcephfs after a non-RESET reclaim; RECLAIM_CLIENT feature required; -ENOENT to the caller when no rank returned an address.
Sessions opened by ceph_start_reclaim after ceph_set_session_timeout carry only metadata['timeout'] (no hostname/root/uuid); they are closed by ceph_set_uuid and reopened by mount with full metadata.
MDS rejects REQUEST_OPEN whose metadata uuid matches an existing session ('duplicated session uuid'); reclaim requires same cephx auth_name.

metadata['timeout'] seconds: considered only after the queue_max_age+session_timeout cutoff, after the session_autoclose eviction check, and (mds_defer_session_stale) only while the MDS revokes caps or awaits a flush; then no stale marking, eviction after queue_max_age+timeout (0 = never by this rule); kept through recovery until reclaimed.

No wire message; conflicting access must revoke one of pAsLsXsFsrc (RD) or Fxwb (WR) from the holder; holder may delay ack up to deleg_timeout (< session_autoclose returned by ceph_get_cap_return_timeout).
LOOKUPINO #ino (args.lookupino.snapid for snapshots) to a random in rank with mount default perms; MDS must locate any inode (open_ino) or return -ESTALE.
fsync = data flush + cap UPDATE with FLAG_SYNC (MDS flushes its journal, FLUSH_ACK after commit) + REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG and wait for safe replies of unsafe ops.
MClientMetrics to rank 0 each tick when rank 0 active and METRIC_COLLECT; payloads selected by MDS metric_spec; includes SUBVOLUME_METRICS aggregated per subvolume id.
FUSE inode = (stag<<48)|ino; MDS inode numbers must be < 2^48.
Client refuses lookups of MDS-private inode numbers (-ESTALE) locally; MDS also returns -ESTALE for them.
inline_version must be > 0 after a GETATTR with CEPH_STAT_CAP_INLINE_DATA (CEPH_INLINE_NONE when not inline); client asserts otherwise.
CEPH_MDS_OP_GETVXATTR only if MDS advertises OP_GETVXATTR; reply extra_bl is a versioned string; -EOPNOTSUPP mapped to -ENODATA.
SETXATTR carries args.setxattr.osdmap_epoch; for layout pool changes the client first waits for the latest OSDMap if the pool is unknown.
args.filelock_change {rule FCNTL/FLOCK(/INTR), type SHARED/EXCL/UNLOCK, owner|1<<63, pid, start, length, wait}; GETFILELOCK reply extra_bl = ceph_filelock.
MCommand sent directly to MDS daemons resolved from FSMap; MCommandReply with rs and data.
FLUSHSNAP_ACK must come from a rank on which the client holds a cap for the inode (ceph_assert in handle_cap_flushsnap_ack; dispatched before the cap lookup).
A cap in a reply/IMPORT whose seq is not newer than the client's cap seq must carry the same cap_id (ceph_assert in add_update_cap).
CEPH_SNAP_OP_SPLIT must set head.split and its trace must start with the split realm (client asserts).

CEPH_CAP_OP_FLUSHSNAP to the auth rank with cap_id 0, seq 0, realm ino, auth mseq, snap_follows, issued/dirty, xattrs always, size/times/change_attr, client_tid, oldest_flush_tid; fscrypt_auth is never filled (fscrypt_file assigned twice).
handle_cap_flush_ack reads flushing_cap_tids.begin() without an emptiness check; an MDS should not send FLUSH_ACK for an inode with no pending flush (C++ MDS re-acks completed flush tids).
insert_readdir_results runs only when the reply trace has is_target (the directory inode); extra_bl of a READDIR/LSSNAP/READDIR_SNAPDIFF reply without it is not decoded.

rust_implications.implication: Keep per-session feature bitsets and choose encodings per session (InodeStat versioned vs legacy, SnapRealmInfoNew vs SnapRealmInfo, openc_response_t, request head versions). libcephfs advertises every bit, the kernel a different subset.
Never send session ops other than OPEN/CLOSE/RENEWCAPS/STALE/RECALL_STATE/FLUSHMSG/FORCE_RO/REJECT to clients and only LEASE_REVOKE lease actions; libcephfs aborts or asserts otherwise.
Count exactly the messages libcephfs counts (caps, lease, snap, quota) per session; do not count quarantine-disable or other new message types, or session close will hang.

Clients address requests relative to arbitrary inode numbers and send LOOKUPINO to random ranks, so every shard/rank needs a fast ino -> owning shard index (and open_ino fallback) independent of path traversal.
Allocate inode numbers below 2^48 (ceph-fuse) and never expose MDS-private ranges.
Answer REQUEST_RENEWCAPS without taking shard locks or waiting on journals; a late ack invalidates every cap of the session on the client and multiplies GETATTR/LOOKUP load.

libcephfs only sends requests to ranks whose MDSMap state is ACTIVE or STOPPING; per-shard recovery must not be exposed as a non-active rank state, and Ganesha 'timeout' sessions currently gate the whole rank in CLIENTREPLAY until reclaimed. A shard-autonomous design must decide how to reproduce that gate (e.g. per shard) while presenting ACTIVE to clients.

Persist session uuid, timeout metadata and cephx auth_name in the new on-disk format so reclaim by uuid works after MDS restarts; implement CEPH_RECLAIM_RESET (kill/evict+blocklist) and FLAG_FINISH; reject duplicate uuids.

rust_implications.topic: QoS classification per request, not per session
rust_implications.implication: A single libcephfs session (Ganesha cmount) multiplexes many NFS clients, users (caller_uid/gid + gid_list) and subvolumes; per-subvolume rate limiting must classify each request by its target inode/subvolume.

Support FLAG_SYNC on cap updates and REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG with sharded journals: flush every journal shard holding the session's unsafe ops or the inode's dirty state, then send FLUSH_ACK / safe replies.
Unsafe replies may be sent before journaling, but the following safe reply must have an empty trace; fsync latency is bounded by the journal shard flush.

Delegations are invisible on the wire; conflicting access by another client must revoke the delegation cap set, and the lock manager must tolerate acks delayed up to the delegation timeout without evicting before session_autoclose.

Clients enforce quotas by walking snap realm parents; every quota directory must appear as a realm root in snap traces and quota/rstat must be pushed (MClientQuota) regardless of internal realm representation.
Preserve dl_dir_hash semantics and return entries per frag in (frag_value(hash), name) order with HASH_ORDER|OFFSET_HASH flags; clients compute offsets themselves and resume by name or offset_hash.

libcephfs sends all metrics (including per-subvolume IO metrics) only to rank 0; per-subvolume SLA tracking across ranks needs rank 0 to aggregate or forward these, or a different metric_spec strategy.
libcephfs flushes dirty caps with CEPH_CAP_OP_UPDATE (not FLUSH); treat any cap message with dirty bits as a flush that needs a FLUSH_ACK with the client tid.

libcephfs performs a LOOKUP (and possibly GETATTR for As) before each create/mkdir/unlink unless the parent dentry cache is authoritative; issuing Fs on directories and dentry leases reduces round trips and same-dir contention.
Trim completed requests using MClientRequest.oldest_client_tid only; libcephfs never transmits oldest_client_tid in RENEWCAPS.
During reconnect accept REPLAY requests with head.ino, re-sent completed requests (answer from completed-request records in clientreplay), and early cap flushes that precede MClientReconnect.
Do not append fields to MClientReply, MClientSnap or MClientQuota payloads (libcephfs asserts on trailing bytes); version new data through existing versioned structures.
Even without inline data support, report inline_version = CEPH_INLINE_NONE in InodeStat and caps; libcephfs asserts if it stays 0.

rust_implications.topic: max_size grants for sync NFS writes
rust_implications.implication: Writers block on max_size growth; grant generous max_size increments proactively to avoid synchronous round trips per extending write.
Userspace bit 22 is CHARMAP while this kernel snapshot uses bit 22 for SUBVOLUME_METRICS; feature interpretation must be explicit per client type/version.
Send cap_auths in CEPH_SESSION_OPEN consistent with MDS enforcement; libcephfs uses them to skip OPEN requests and buffer setattr locally.
If DELEG_INO is advertised to a session, always encode create replies' extra_bl as openc_response_t (even with no delegated inos); libcephfs chooses the decoder from the advertised bit.

rust_implications.topic: Cap message invariants checked by client asserts
rust_implications.implication: Only send FLUSHSNAP_ACK from a rank that still holds a cap for the client, never change cap_id without advancing seq, and start SPLIT traces with the split realm; these are crash conditions for unmodified libcephfs.

Ganesha cmounts and libcephfsd (Samba proxy) concentrate many applications and users on one session per rank; per-client limits, cap recall and QoS should be designed for sessions carrying thousands of concurrent requests and out-of-order tids.

If REQUEST_CLOSE stays deferred until a rank is ACTIVE, ceph_set_uuid of a restarting Ganesha can time out while other reclaims hold the rank; consider processing closes during CLIENTREPLAY or scoping the reclaim gate.

open_questions: Ganesha FSAL_CEPH call patterns (which ceph_ll_* calls, nonblocking IO usage, mapping of NFS COMMIT/FILE_SYNC to fsync, cmount sharing policy, client_permissions setting) cannot be verified from this repository.
Kernel bit 22 (CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS in the kernel snapshot) collides with userspace CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP; which interpretation should a new MDS use for kernel sessions?
Runtime effect of MQuarantineDisable being counted by the MDS but not by libcephfs (expected: REQUEST_CLOSE dropped and unmount waits client_shutdown_timeout).
Does the Rust MDS need to support pre-REPLY_ENCODING (pre-Nautilus) libcephfs clients and the legacy request head?
Should the new MDS keep the rank-wide CLIENTREPLAY gate for sessions with 'timeout' metadata, or can reclaim gating be scoped to the subtrees/shards those sessions held caps in?
libcephfs does not retry -EAGAIN from fscrypt truncate (stale last-block change_attr); is that the intended application-visible behavior?
Client::_kick_stale_sessions appears not to advance its iterator for OPEN sessions; is the asok/auto-reconnect path used in production?
Metadata latency metrics from libcephfs mix CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC; should the new MDS ignore or sanitize them?

With mds_allow_async_dirops=false the C++ MDS sends a raw u64 created ino while advertising DELEG_INO; does libcephfs really mis-decode (exception) at runtime, and should the new MDS ever advertise DELEG_INO without openc_response_t?
Should libcephfsd-shared mounts (Samba proxy) be treated as a distinct client class for session limits and recall?
